title: destroy on the last sandbox of a named group leaves the group's network, keepalive and gateway running, and says nothing
foundBy: session agent replaying a multi-member campaign through cs-vcr, several replays at a time on one shared host
details:
**What happened.** A person typed four commands by hand: `create <name> --group <group>`, `exec`, `fetch` and `destroy <name>.<group> --force`. The destroy printed `destroyed <name>.<group>` and nothing more. The host still held the group's keepalive container and its network. They were gone once the person ran `cs-sandbox group rm <group>`.

**Why it matters.** `create --group` makes the group when it is needed, so the person never typed a command that made one. Nothing tells them that `destroy` does not undo it. A named group that holds no sandbox is rarely wanted, and each one keeps a container, a network and a tap prefix.

**What is asked for.** When `destroy` empties a group other than `default`, print one line that names `cs-sandbox group rm <group>`. `destroy --dry-run` could list the same. Removing the emptied group automatically is the other choice, and it is a larger change in behaviour.

**How to reproduce.** Run `cs-sandbox create a --group g`, then `cs-sandbox destroy a.g --force`, then `podman ps` and `podman network ls`.
